newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen tops Shanghai in listings in first half.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen tops Shanghai in listings in first half.

text.p: The Shenzhen Stock Exchange beat its counterpart in Shanghai in the listing of new shares in the first half of 1997, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Thursday.
In the January-June period of this year, Shenzhen listed 90 stocks and Shanghai floated only 49, the newspaper said.
The 139 newcomers listed a total of 7.108 billion shares and raised total proceeds of 49.058 billion yuan, it said.
By the end of June, the Shenzhen exchange had 360 listed stocks compared with 388 in Shanghai, the newspaper said.
Total market capitalisation on the two exchanges had reached 1,666.47 billion yuan by end-June, it said.
About 80 percent of companies listed in the first half were medium- or large-scale state enterprises mainly from such sectors as raw materials, communications and energy, the newspaper said.
In addition, nearly 50 percent of the newcomers are based in the center or western part of China, a contrast to earlier listings of enterprises based mainly in coastal areas, it said.
